A q-round EF matching strategy reduces every first-order sentence to finitely many capped independent Poisson counts. Singleton marked classes prove the supercritical endpoint. value.rationale: A natural independently sparsified equivalence-class model exhibits a precise nondegenerate logical phase transition at the Lambert-W scale. The theorem gives not just a yes/no threshold but the full independently sized Poisson defect process and an effective probability algorithm for every fixed first-order sentence, with analytic parameter dependence. This connects randomly marked partitions to the recent study of logic of random expansions and goes beyond an arbitrary finite invariant or an isolated moment calculation.
